definition: Subvocal recognition (SVR) is the process of taking subvocalization and converting the detected results to a digital output, aural or text-based.
details: A silent speech interface is a device that allows speech communication without using the sound made when people vocalize their speech sounds. It works by the computer identifying the phonemes that an individual pronounces from nonauditory sources of information about their speech movements. These are then used to recreate the speech using speech synthesis.

explainer.lead: Subvocal recognition takes subvocalisation and converts the detected results to a digital output, aural or text-based. It matters as the basis of silent speech interfaces that allow communication without vocalising speech sounds.

tiers.eli5: It is a system that reads the tiny silent movements you make when you 'say' words in your head and turns them into speech or text.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers capture speech movements via ultrasound or optical cameras on tongue and lips, electromagnetic tracking, electromyography of speech articulator muscles and the larynx, non-audible murmurs through bone conduction, or motor-cortex brain activity from intracortical microelectrodes. The computer identifies phonemes from these nonauditory sources and recreates speech by speech synthesis.
tiers.paperLevel: A silent speech interface identifies the phonemes an individual pronounces from nonauditory information about speech movements, then recreates the speech using speech synthesis; input methods include ultrasound, optical camera, electromagnetic, electromyography, non-audible murmurs and brain-computer interface.

explainer.example: Electromyography of speech articulator muscles captures a silently mouthed word, and speech synthesis outputs it as audible speech.

usedIn.name: Assistive technology
